# Command Flags

Each command's `--help`, as agent-desktop 1.1.0 prints it, without the
flags the app sets itself or refuses. A command's own section leaves out the
options every command takes, listed first.

## Options for every command

```
Options:
      --headed                         Prefer physical delivery for natural input commands and permit focus/cursor side effects. Default is strict headless semantic delivery.
  -w, --wait-for <WAIT_FOR>            Poll until an element matching the role:text selector appears, then return the snapshot (snapshot and ref actions only)
      --wait-for-gone <WAIT_FOR_GONE>  Poll until no element matches the role:text selector, then return the snapshot (snapshot and ref actions only)
      --wait-timeout <WAIT_TIMEOUT>    Maximum wait time in milliseconds for --wait-for / --wait-for-gone (default: 30000)
```

## snapshot

```
Capture accessibility tree as structured JSON with @ref IDs

Usage: agent-desktop snapshot [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --app <APP>                      Filter to application by name
      --window-id <window-id>          Scope to a single window ID (from list-windows)
      --max-depth <MAX_DEPTH>          Maximum tree depth (default 10) [default: 10]
      --include-bounds                 Include element bounds (x, y, width, height)
  -i, --interactive-only               Include interactive elements only
      --compact                        Collapse single-child unnamed nodes to reduce tree depth
      --skeleton                       Shallow overview with children_count on truncated containers
      --surface <SURFACE>              Surface to snapshot [default: window] [possible values: window, focused, menu, menubar, sheet, popover, alert, desktop, taskbar, system-tray, quick-settings, notification-center, toolbar, dock, spotlight, menu-bar-extras, system-tray-overflow, start-menu, action-center]
      --root <ROOT>                    Start traversal from this ref instead of window root
      --timeout-ms <MS>                Observation deadline in milliseconds (default 3000; raise for slow Chromium settles)
      --force-electron-a11y            Assume Chromium renderer accessibility is forced (skips activation guidance)
```

## find

```
Search elements by role, name, value, or text content

Usage: agent-desktop find [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --app <APP>                      Filter to application by name
      --window-id <window-id>          Scope to a single window ID (from list-windows)
      --role <ROLE>                    Match by accessibility role (button, textfield, checkbox ...)
      --name <NAME>                    Match by accessible name or label
      --value <VALUE>                  Match by current value
      --text <TEXT>                    Match by text in name, value, title, or description
      --description <DESCRIPTION>      Match by accessible description
      --native-id <NATIVE_ID>          Match by native automation id (AXIdentifier)
      --exact                          Require exact (case-insensitive) name/description/value matches
      --root <ROOT>                    Search only inside this ref's subtree, not the whole window
      --surface <SURFACE>              Surface to search (menubar, menu, sheet ...) instead of the window [default: window] [possible values: window, focused, menu, menubar, sheet, popover, alert, desktop, taskbar, system-tray, quick-settings, notification-center, toolbar, dock, spotlight, menu-bar-extras, system-tray-overflow, start-menu, action-center]
      --state <TOKEN[=BOOL]>           Filter by state token (repeatable); append =true or =false
      --timeout-ms <MS>                Traversal deadline in milliseconds (default 5000; raise for a large tree such as a shell file dialog)
      --count                          Return match count only
      --first                          Return first match only
      --last                           Return last match only
      --nth <NTH>                      Return Nth match (0-indexed)
      --limit <LIMIT>                  Return at most N matches; defaults to 50 when omitted, use 0 for all
```

```

Options:

```

## get

```

Usage: agent-desktop get [OPTIONS] <REF>
```


## type

```
Insert text into a text target

Usage: agent-desktop type [OPTIONS] <REF> <TEXT>

Arguments:
  <REF>   Qualified ref from snapshot (@<snapshot_id>:eN)
  <TEXT>  Text to type

Options:
      --timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>        Maximum wait in milliseconds, covering ref resolution, actionability and delivery of the text; default 5000 plus 30 per character of TEXT; 0 disables the wait
      --interval-ms <INTERVAL_MS>      Type one keystroke every N ms (1-2000) instead of inserting TEXT at once; --timeout-ms then applies to each keystroke, and 0 makes each keystroke try once
```

## press

```
Send a key combo: return, escape, cmd+c, shift+tab ...

Usage: agent-desktop press [OPTIONS] <COMBO>

Arguments:
  <COMBO>  Key combo: return, escape, cmd+c, shift+tab ...

Options:
      --app <APP>                      Target application name; keys go to its process without focusing it (--headed focuses its window first)
      --window-id <WINDOW_ID>          Target the application instance that owns this window (from list-windows); use it when several instances share one name
```

## key-down

```
Hold a key or modifier down

Usage: agent-desktop key-down [OPTIONS] <COMBO>

Arguments:
  <COMBO>  Key or modifier to hold/release: shift, meta, ctrl ... (cmd is accepted); the command is rejected in stateless mode, use press instead

Options:
      --force                          Send the combo even if the adapter flags it as a dangerous shortcut
```

```

Usage: agent-desktop key-up [OPTIONS] <COMBO>
```

## hover

```
Move cursor to element center or coordinates (requires --headed)

Usage: agent-desktop hover [OPTIONS] [REF]

Arguments:
  [REF]  Element ref to hover over; requires --headed

Options:
      --xy <XY>                        Absolute coordinates as x,y; requires --headed; write a negative value with = (--xy=-100,50)
      --duration <DURATION>            Reserved for compatibility; positive values are rejected in stateless mode (run hover, then `wait <ms>` instead)
      --timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>        Maximum ref-resolution and transient-actionability wait in milliseconds; terminal failures return immediately [default: 5000]
```

## drag

```
Drag from one element or point to another (requires --headed)

Usage: agent-desktop drag [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --from <FROM>                    Source element ref; requires --headed
      --from-xy <from-xy>              Source coordinates as x,y; requires --headed; write a negative value with = (--from-xy=-100,50)
      --to <TO>                        Destination element ref; requires --headed
      --to-xy <to-xy>                  Destination coordinates as x,y; requires --headed; write a negative value with = (--to-xy=-100,50)
      --duration <DURATION>            Drag duration in milliseconds
      --drop-delay <MS>                Hold over the destination this many ms before releasing, so the drop target activates; default 500 (150 on Linux)
      --timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>        Drag action budget in milliseconds, including resolution, actionability, pickup, duration and drop delay; allow headroom for completion [default: 5000]
      --wait-for-scope <SCOPE>         Window a drag's --wait-for/--wait-for-gone verification polls: 'to' (drop target, default) or 'from' (pickup). Needed when the confirmation appears only in the destination window of a cross-window drag [possible values: from, to]
```

## mouse-wheel

```
Scroll the mouse wheel at absolute coordinates (requires --headed)

Usage: agent-desktop mouse-wheel [OPTIONS] --x <X> --y <Y>

Options:
      --x <X>                          Absolute X coordinate for wheel event; write a negative value with = (--x=-100)
      --y <Y>                          Absolute Y coordinate for wheel event; write a negative value with = (--y=-100)
      --dy <DY>                        Vertical wheel lines; positive scrolls up, negative scrolls down (default -3 when --dx is absent, else 0)
      --dx <DX>                        Horizontal wheel lines; positive scrolls right, negative scrolls left [default: 0]
      --modifiers <MODIFIER>           Held modifiers: shift, meta, ctrl, alt (repeatable; cmd is accepted)
```

## launch

```
Launch application and return once its process is running; --activate waits for a window, --cdp verifies a DevTools endpoint

Usage: agent-desktop launch [OPTIONS] <APP>

Arguments:
  <APP>  Application name or bundle ID

Options:
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>              Upper bound in ms for the whole launch [default: 30000]
      --no-attach                      Start a fresh instance instead of attaching to a running one (Windows fails if the app is already running)
      --activate                       Bring the app forward so it presents a window, and wait for one
```

## wait

```
Wait for time (ms), element presence, text, or window appearance

Usage: agent-desktop wait [OPTIONS] [MS]

Arguments:
  [MS]  Milliseconds to pause

Options:
      --element <ELEMENT>              Block until this element ref appears in the tree
      --window <WINDOW>                Block until a window with this title appears; with --event, narrows the event wait to that window title instead of selecting a mode
      --text <TEXT>                    Block until text appears in the app's accessibility tree; with --notification, filter notification text
      --menu                           Block until a menu surface is open
      --menu-closed                    Block until the menu surface is dismissed
      --notification                   Block until a new notification arrives
      --event <EVENT>                  Block until a desktop lifecycle signal, detected by baseline diff without needing to know the id/title up front: window-opened, window-closed, app-launched, app-terminated, focus-changed, surface-appeared, surface-dismissed
      --window-id <window-id>          Optional: narrow --event window-opened/window-closed/focus-changed to one window ID
      --predicate <PREDICATE>          Element wait predicate: exists, enabled, visible, actionable, or value
      --value <VALUE>                  Expected value for --predicate value
      --action <ACTION>                Action for --predicate actionable: click (default), type, set-value, or clear
      --count <COUNT>                  Expected match count for --text waits
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>              Timeout in milliseconds for element/window/text waits [default: 30000]
      --app <APP>                      Scope element, window, or text wait to this application
```

## skills

```
Bundled skill docs for AI agents (list, get, path)

Usage: agent-desktop skills [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list  List bundled skills with summaries (default)
  get   Print a skill (markdown in data.content)
  path  Print where bundled skills live
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:

Skills are compiled into the binary, so they always match this exact
agent-desktop version. Each command prints the JSON envelope; the skill's
markdown is in data.content.

Start here:
  agent-desktop skills get desktop            # Core guide, any OS
  agent-desktop skills get platform           # Guide for the OS you run on

More:
  agent-desktop skills                        # List skills
  agent-desktop skills get desktop workflows  # One reference
  agent-desktop skills get windows            # A named platform guide
  agent-desktop skills path                   # Where skills live
```
